policy_title: Sewage Tax on Water Company Profits
stated: Tackle the national scandal of sewage-polluted rivers, waterways and beaches, and make water companies work for people by: Introducing a Sewage Tax on water company profits. Enforcing existing laws to ensure that the storm overflows only function in exceptional circumstances. Setting legally binding targets to prevent sewage dumping into bathing waters and highly sensitive nature sites by 2030. Embracing nature-based solutions to tackle the problem of sewage dumping.

bearing_set.reason: Directly targets sewage pollution in rivers, waterways and beaches — a core water quality indicator under Clean Environment.

A tax on water company profits in a regulated monopoly sector creates a plausible cost-passthrough mechanism: if Ofwat accommodates it in future price reviews, household water bills — an essential — rise, directly affecting the cost-of-essentials basket.

Introducing a new sector-specific profits tax is a material fiscal measure; the net effect on public finances (revenue raised versus enforcement/nature-based-solutions costs) is a real, non-negligible verdict on the funded vs. borrowed balance.

membership_note: Three genuine bearings: O6 is the designed-for outcome (water and nature quality); O2 captures the regulated-utility cost-passthrough risk to household water bills; O12 captures the fiscal materiality of a new profits tax instrument. Effects on O13 (infrastructure investment) and O4 are too attenuated to clear the non-negligible bar without a more specific mechanism.
